findings.text: The check calls `Error(t, panicErr)` and `EqualError(t, ...)`, and both call `Fail(t)` themselves on failure. A mismatch is therefore reported twice, once by `EqualError` and again by the outer `Fail`. For example, `PanicsWithError(t, "x", func(){ panic(errors.New("y")) })` records two failures on `t`, and any caller that counts failures or errors sees extra ones. Compare `panicErr.Error() != errString` directly, so only the one `Fail` runs.
